details: The European Central Bank (ECB) has expressed strong skepticism regarding plans to expand the euro stablecoin market. President Christine Lagarde and other central bankers warn that increased adoption of stablecoins could pose significant risks to financial stability and undermine the effectiveness of monetary policy by potentially diverting funds from traditional bank deposits and complicating interest rate transmission. The ECB reportedly favors tokenized bank deposits over privately issued stablecoins.
title: ECB Warns Against Euro Stablecoin Expansion, Citing Financial Stability Concerns

details: The U.S. dollar experienced losses as investor optimism grew regarding a potential deal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz and end the conflict in Iran. While a near-term resolution is considered unlikely by some analysts, hopes for peace have pushed oil prices below $100 a barrel, eased pressure on emerging-market currencies, and generally boosted risk sentiment. However, fresh U.S. strikes on Iranian targets introduced some caution.
title: Dollar Wobbles as Markets Hope for Middle East Peace Deal

details: American consumer sentiment has dropped to one of its lowest points in history, reflecting persistent concerns about high prices, softening employment, and geopolitical instability, particularly the conflict involving Iran. Despite this, the stock market, including the S&P 500 and Dow Jones Industrial Average, has continued to climb, raising questions about a potential disconnect between market performance and economic reality for households. Some economists attribute the market's strength to optimism around artificial intelligence.
title: US Consumer Sentiment Plummets as Stock Market Continues to Rally
